scripts.//build:core: Unlike @taproot/astro, which ships source and is compiled by the host's Vite pipeline, @taproot/core is consumed as compiled `dist/` — its exports map points there, and the seed/migrate scripts import it under plain node. Nothing but `npm install` (via prepare) and `npm run build` ever ran tsc, so editing core and running dev served the *previous* compile: the missing symbol surfaces as `@taproot/core does not provide an export named X`, which reads like the export was never written rather than never rebuilt. Hence the pre-hooks below on every entry point that loads core. Incremental `tsc --build` is ~0.2s when up to date.
scripts.build: npm run build --workspace=@taproot/core && npm run build --workspace=@taproot/web
scripts.//typecheck: Per-workspace rather than a root `tsc --build`: there is no root tsconfig, and the two Astro-facing projects cannot be tsc project references — apps/web's sources are .astro, which tsc has no resolver for. apps/web is type-checked by `npm run build` instead.
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck --workspace=@taproot/core && npm run typecheck --workspace=@taproot/astro
scripts.//taproot:types: Generates apps/web/src/content.d.ts from the live content model, read over the delivery API rather than out of the database — so the types describe what a consumer actually receives. Needs a running server; set TAPROOT_API_URL and TAPROOT_API_KEY for anything but local dev.
scripts.//docs: The handbook. A separate Astro app with no database and no admin, so it builds and deploys on its own — and so the demo site stays a demo rather than doubling as the product's documentation. Port 4322 keeps it clear of `npm run dev`.
